NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  In accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361), City Council Resolution Nos. 2487, 2490, 2491, 2493,
  2498, 2499, 2503, and proposed Resolution No. 2505, due to the continuing state of emergency, including
  masking and social distancing directives as a result of the threat of the COVID-19 virus, this meeting is
  being broadcast via teleconference.  Members of the public may participate in-person in the Council
  Chambers, or virtually in the meeting in the following ways:

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1 669 900 6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 886 8396 8052 Meeting Password: 066081. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails
  received before 3:00 p.m. prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record.

  - Members of the public may also comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 886 8396 8052, Meeting Password: 066081. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  APRIL 26, 2022

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR ZERUNYAN at 7:05 pm in the Council Chambers of City Hall and remotely via
teleconference, in accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361) and City Council Resolution
Nos. 2487, 2490, 2491, 2493, 2498, 2499, 2503 and proposed Resolution No. 2505, due to
the continuing state of emergency, including masking and social distancing directives as a
result of the threat of the COVID-19 virus.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by Rolling Robots members Morgan Deng and Winston Lin.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Community Development & PW Director David Wahba
  Planning Manager Jeannie Naughton
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Management Analyst Jessica Slawson
  Administrative Aide Gabrielle Swain

4.  CEREMONIAL

A.  RECOGNITION OF LOCAL STATE CHAMPIONS, ROLLING ROBOTS

MAYOR ZERUNYAN introduced and presented Certificates of Recognition for the following
teams and members of Rolling Robots:

  -  Team 7700E - Tournament Champions: Austin Chen, Ronojoy Sen, Madeleine
  Jiang, Nikhil Ramanuja, Renee Gerstner, Morgan Deng, Aidan Westerland
  -  Team 92305A - Tournament Champions: Timmy Brennan, Troy So, Rainelle
  Yasa, Winston Lin, Zain Mourad, Leo Lopez, Leopoldo Gastel, Max Waldman
  -  Team 7700K - Tournament Finalist and Create Award Winner: Ashley Wills,
  Thomas Wang, Noah Kim, Chris Campbell, Kyle Chu, Daniel Hong
  -  Team 7700R - Sportsmanship Award Winner: Benjamin Lee, Jaehoon Kim, Avery
  Lam, Matthew Kwon, Sean Magers, Saifali Haji, Joshua Roe
  -  Team 7700V - Design Award: Alex Cao, Liam Horeczko, Lawrence Hui, Anthony
  Hui, Charlie Pan

B.  PROCLAMATION DECLARING APRIL 24, 2022 AS A DAY OF REMEMBRANCE
  OF THE ARMENIAN GENOCIDE OF 1915-1923

MAYOR ZERUNYAN presented a proclamation declaring April 24, 2022 as a day of
remembrance of the Armenian Genocide of 1915-1923, and provided a presentation on the
history of the Armenian Genocide.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good

  Recommendation: That the City Council (1) Re-open the Public Hearing; (2) Take

  SCHMITZ, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2497, ADOPTING THE ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES 2040 GENERAL PLAN AND 2021-2029 HOUSING ELEMENT.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN read Resolution No. 2497 by title.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
APRIL 26, 2022
 MAYOR ZERUNYAN thanked COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ and COUNCIL MEMBER
ZUCKERMAN for chairing the GPAC, COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA for being a member
of the GPAC, and staff.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN thanked all consultants involved, in addition to Planning
Manager Naughton and Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  RESOLUTION NO. 2506 - AMENDING THE CITY’S FINE SCHEDULE FOR
  ADMINISTRATIVE CITATIONS TO ESTABLISH A SPECIAL FINE AMOUNT FOR
  VIOLATIONS OF SECTIONS 9.04.040 AND 12.24.110 OF THE ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE PERTAINING TO THE POSSESSION AND
  DISCHARGE OF FIREWORKS

  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt Resolution 2506, amending the City’s
  fine schedule for administrative citations to establish a special fine amount for violations
  of sections 9.04.040 and 12.24.110 of the Rolling Hills Estates Municipal Code.

Management Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ reported on the discussion had by the Equestrian
Committee regarding firework use in the landfill and how last year’s efforts were fantastic in
suppressing firework use. She also commented that she hopes a $1,000 fine is enough to
deter people, stressing that the City is a high-fire zone and how dangerous a potential fire
could be for the Peninsula, and that fires do not stop at jurisdictional lines.

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF commented that firework use has increased over the last few
years, occurring year-round, and that she is eager to support this Resolution.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA echoed MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF, noting that fireworks
can be heard year-round. She suggested year-round signs stating “You are entering a high-
fire risk area”, for those entering and visiting the community. She inquired if this was a
service offered by Cal Fire, and stated that it could be a cost-sharing opportunity with the
other Peninsula cities if not offered by Cal Fire. City Manager Grammer stated that staff
would explore various options for signs and bring the findings back to Council.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No additional public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  ADOPT RESOLUTION 2506, AMENDING THE CITY’S FINE SCHEDULE
  FOR ADMINISTRATIVE CITATIONS TO ESTABLISH A SPECIAL FINE
  AMOUNT FOR VIOLATIONS OF SECTIONS 9.04.040 AND 12.24.110 OF
  THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

City Clerk Pettit read Resolution No. 2506 by title.

B.  REVIEW OF PROPOSED AMENDMENTS TO MUNICIPAL CODE CHAPTER 17.60
  (SIGNS)

  Recommendation: That the City Council (1) review the proposed amendments to
  Municipal Code Chapter 17.60 and provide direction; and (2) unless further Council
  review is desired, direct staff to proceed with a formal ordinance for presentation to
  the Planning Commission.

City Attorney Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
APRIL 26, 2022
 City Attorney Davis clarified that a pole sign is a form of a free standing sign, in response to
COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ inquired about the school/student accolade signs that have
become popular on residential lawns during the pandemic, stating that there should be sign
education for residents who wouldn’t otherwise know these rules and requirements within the
City’s code.

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF noted that enforcement of sign regulations has been primarily
complaint-based.

City Attorney Davis explained the definition of “temporary,” in response to COUNCIL
MEMBER ZUCKERMAN. COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN inquired if HOAs could deny
a sign that would otherwise be accepted under the City’s sign code. City Attorney Davis
confirmed that would be possible, depending on how the HOA went about it.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ discussed the possibility of window signs in commercial
buildings being used as a safety or security measure, in addition to advertising.

City Attorney confirmed that the authority to remove abandoned signs is included in the
proposed code amendment, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN.

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba confirmed a licensed sign installer
would be required and that all lighted signs are now required to be LED, in response to
COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN. COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN also suggested
requiring primer in addition to paint on the sign boxes.

City Attorney Davis explained that temporary banner permits are not changed or regulated
by this code amendment, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ, AS
  FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  DIRECT STAFF TO PROCEED WITH A FORMAL ORDINANCE FOR
  PRESENTATION TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

**ITEM TAKEN OUT OF ORDER**

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  REQUEST FOR THREE-MONTH EXTENSION OF A SPECIAL EVENT PERMIT
  (SEP) GRANTED TO ROLLING HILLS COVENANT CHURCH (RHCC).
  LOCATION: 2222 PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH
  APPLICANT: ROBERT CUBILLOS C/O OF RHCC

  Recommendation: That the City Council conduct a hearing for the Rolling Hills
  Covenant Church (RHCC) requested three-month extension of their Special Event
  Permit (SEP) for the continued use of their outdoor parking lot tent, granted by the
  City Council on January 25, 2022, which would extend their Permit from May 1 to July
  31, 2022; and, take one of the staff recommended actions as listed above in this
  report.

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the
agenda material).

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
APRIL 26, 2022
 Craig Knickerbocker of RHCC spoke regarding the extension request, and also suggested a
new option for consideration involving moving the current tent to the front parking lot of the
Church.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA confirmed that the same tent would be moved from the front
to back of the property. She also asked Mr. Knickerbocker to outline the renovation timeline,
which was scheduled to be completed by May 1.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
Public testimony was received by resident Michael Goodin against the extension request,
resident Bridget Carman against the extension request, and resident Debra Fixen against the
extension request.

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba explained that moving the tent to
the front of the property would likely cause new noise issues for the neighbors across Palos
Verdes Drive North in the Montecillo and Casaba neighborhoods.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ emphasized the importance of residents being able to enjoy
their private space, stating that grace was given to the Church due the circumstances
brought on by COVID, and that she was not in favor of continuing any amplified sound going
forward.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN stated that he was in favor of option 2 of the staff
recommendation as a fair compromise.

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF stated she was not opposed to option 2, and also suggested
allowing the Church the opportunity to try moving the tent to the front of the property for a
trial weekend.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA emphasized that the Special Event Permit was not issued
to accommodate a remodel of the sanctuary, it was issued to protect the public health of
those who attend the Church during the pandemic. She made a motion to approve option 2
of the staff recommendation, granting the extension without any amplified sound, and
allowing for no further extensions of the permit.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN thanked the residents who provided comments, as well as the Church.

Discussion ensued about the use of amplified sound, versus prohibiting the use of amplified
music.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA amended her motion, to prohibit the use of amplified sound
for music.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ, AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  GRANT RHCC REQUESTED THREE-MONTH EXTENSION OF SPECIAL
  EVENT PERMIT TO EXPIRE ON JULY 31, 2022, USING THE SAME
  CONDITIONS ON THE PERMIT GRANTED ON JANUARY 25, 2022, BUT
  WITHOUT THE USE OF AMPLIFIED SOUND FOR THE MUSICAL PORTIONS
  OF THE SERVICE, AND NO OPTION TO EXTEND THE EXISTING PERMIT.

  AYES:  Huff, Stegura, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
